title: Long-term assessment of social amplification of risk during COVID-19: challenges to public health agencies amid misinformation and vaccine stance
screen_reason: Observational Twitter study of 1,683,700 Finnish vaccination-related tweets (Dec 2019 - Oct 2022) that reports the share of tweets classified as containing misinformation (460,087, 27.3%), the share of engagements with the Finnish public health agency account carrying misinformation/negative vaccine stance, the share of ordinary users' retweets originating from malicious bot accounts, and a concentration statement (the vocal 10% of users account for over 82% of MINVS content). Several quantitative shares with stated denominators, so eligible. The classifier-building part is instrumental, not the study's claim, so the 'detection/classifier work' exclusion does not apply.

estimates.measure_type: % of collected vaccination-related tweets classified as containing misinformation
estimates.denominator: 1,683,700 Finnish-language tweets (724,214 retweets, 57,865 quotes, 901,621 original tweets) from 60,560 unique accounts, collected with 147 query keywords built from 14 Finnish corona/vaccine terms
estimates.definition: Tweet classified into the 'misinformation' class by a fine-tuned FinBERT model trained on 4,150 manually annotated tweets, using the Memon and Carley misinformation codebook (conspiracy theories, counterfeit treatments/cures, panic buying etc.), with codebook criteria adapted to 2022 and supported by fact-checking sites including THL pages
estimates.misinfo_def: misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information that is intentionally or unintentionally disseminated
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Fine-tuned FinBERT classifier trained on 4,150 randomly sampled tweets manually annotated by four Finnish-speaking research assistants after six rounds of training; Krippendorff's alpha 0.668 for misinformation (0.693 for vaccine stance), which the authors themselves describe as only tentatively reliable. No classifier accuracy/F1 is reported in the main text (referred to Online Appendix).
estimates.moderator_quote: We extracted vaccination-related conversations from Twitter (https://twitter.com) between December 1st, 2019, and October 24th, 2022. From a set of 14 Finnish terms, 147 query keywords were constructed using word compounding and variation. Our keyword strategy focuses primarily on the misinformation and vaccine-related views surrounding the COVID-19 debate in Finland.
estimates.notes: Denominator is the keyword corpus as collected, so it includes retweets and quotes as separate items; the share is therefore of tweet events, not of unique messages. The keyword strategy is explicitly skewed towards misinformation and vaccine views ('Our keyword strategy focuses primarily on the misinformation and vaccine-related views'), which inflates the prevalence relative to all COVID/vaccine talk. Data collection spans Dec 2019 - Oct 2022; year coded as the midpoint 2021. Full sentence in the paper (hyphenated across a line break, so only the contiguous fragment is quoted): 'The misinformation classification model further identified 460,087 tweets (27.3%) as containing misinformation.'

estimates.platform: Twitter (engagements targeting the @THLorg public health agency account)
estimates.date: 1 October 2020 - 24 October 2022 (period after the October 2020 breakpoint)
estimates.measure_type: median daily % of engagements (retweets and mentions) with the public health agency account that contained misinformation or negative vaccine stance
estimates.value_raw: median MINVS engagement ratio 6.8% (1 Dec 2019 - 1 Oct 2020), increased to 33.3% from 1 Oct 2020 onwards; neutral engagement ratio 98.8% then 67.2%
estimates.denominator: All daily engagements (retweets and mentions) targeting the THL Twitter account within the 1,683,700-tweet vaccination corpus; ratio computed per day and summarised by its median
estimates.definition: An engagement counts if the retweet or mention targeting THL was classified as containing misinformation OR negative vaccine stance (MINVS), from any account type
estimates.misinfo_def: misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information that is intentionally or unintentionally disseminated, while a negative vaccine stance is defined as the intentional avoidance of vaccination, regardless of the reason for the avoidance
estimates.n: daily engagements with the THL account (denominator size not stated as a single number; average 23.77 daily MINVS engagements)
estimates.source_quote: MINVS engagement ratio is 6.8%. From the 1st of October 2020 onwards, this number increased to 33.3%.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same fine-tuned FinBERT misinformation and stance classifiers (Krippendorff's alpha 0.668 and 0.693 on the 4,150 human-annotated training sample)
estimates.moderator_quote: We defined MINVS engagement as any retweets or mentions that contain either misinformation or negative vaccine sentiment targeting the THL account from all account types.
estimates.notes: BORDERLINE and flagged for adjudication on two grounds. (1) The numerator is a UNION of misinformation and negative vaccine stance, and a negative vaccine stance on its own is an attitude, not misinformation, so this over-states misinformation alone. (2) The value is the MEDIAN of daily ratios, not a pooled share of items; the authors chose the median because single-interaction days inflate the mean. Later of the two time periods taken as the representative point (the earlier period value is 6.8%). Denominator is engagement with ONE account (THL), so this is not a platform-wide share. Source quote is de-hyphenated across a line break ('this num-/ber'), hence quote_verbatim=false; the sentence opens 'Between the 1st of December 2019 and the 1st of October 2020, the median[footnote 4] MINVS engagement ratio is 6.8%.'

estimates.measure_type: % of retweets by human (non-bot) accounts whose original author was a malicious bot (unreliable source)
estimates.value_raw: average retweet from malicious bot ratio is 0.23% in the early stages; from June 2021 a rise (from 0.23 to 3%); the ratio 'consistently remains below 5%'
estimates.denominator: All retweets made by non-bot (human) accounts within the same time frame in the Finnish vaccination corpus (excluding the THL account)
estimates.definition: Retweet counts in the numerator when its original author is one of the 4,894 accounts classified as a malicious bot, i.e. a bot account that spreads misinformation or negative vaccine stance with intent to influence the conversation
estimates.misinfo_def: We defined a malicious account as a bot account that spreads MINVS intending to influence Twitter conversations
estimates.n: non-bot retweets in the corpus (denominator size not stated numerically; corpus contains 724,214 retweets in total)
estimates.source_quote: This trend is particularly evident in the early stages of the pandemic, during which the average retweet from malicious bot ratio is 0.23%. However, from June 2021, there is an observable rise in this ratio (from 0.23 to 3%), indicating some regular users are influenced by the content from malicious bots.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Botometer v4 (CAP >= 0.804, equivalent bot score >= 0.43) to flag bot-like accounts, then an author-built penalty score combining the account's MINVS ratio, COVID-tweet ratio, account age relative to the first Finnish COVID case, and account status; total score > 0.5 = malicious bot. No validation of the malicious-bot rule against human judgement is reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: Retweet ratios are computed by determining the proportion of retweets originating from non-bot users, where the original authors are either the malicious bots (subplot 1) or THL (subplot 2), relative to the total number of retweets observed during the same time frame within the non-bot retweet activity data.
estimates.notes: Source-level, not claim-level: the numerator is retweets of accounts on an author-built 'malicious bot' list, so it is an unreliable-source share rather than a verified-false-content share; breadth left blank accordingly. Time series collapsed to the later period (from June 2021, ratio ~3%); the Jan-Oct 2020 average is 0.23% and the series is said to stay below 5% throughout. Both endpoints are stated verbatim; the mid-period pooled value is not reported. The comparison figure in the same plot (average retweet-from-THL ratio 19% early, 0.8% later) is a reliable-source share and is not a misinformation estimate.

estimates.measure_type: share of all misinformation / negative-vaccine-stance content contributed by the most vocal 10% of users
estimates.value_raw: over 82% of the MINVS contents from our dataset are shared by the vocal minority (the 'loud' 10%)
estimates.conc_group_label: The vocal minority (the 'loud' 10%) of online users, predominantly anti-vaccination campaigners and malicious bots
estimates.denominator: All MINVS (misinformation or negative vaccine stance) content in the corpus of 1,683,700 Finnish vaccination-related tweets from 60,560 unique accounts
estimates.definition: Share of MINVS posts authored/shared by the top 10% most vocal users in the dataset
estimates.misinfo_def: misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information that is intentionally or unintentionally disseminated
estimates.source_quote: the vocal 10% of online users were predominantly anti-vaccination campaigners and malicious bots. In fact, over 82% of the MINVS contents from our dataset are shared by the vocal minority.
estimates.page_loc: Discussion, Influential actors in networks, p. 829
estimates.ground_truth_detail: MINVS labels from the fine-tuned FinBERT misinformation and stance classifiers; the 'vocal 10%' cut-off is imported from prior literature on the 'loud 10%' and its operationalisation (activity threshold) is not spelled out in the text
estimates.moderator_quote: This is also confirmed by previous studies that only a small percentage of individuals participate actively in online discussions, with the majority merely observing the debates. Focusing solely on the vocal minority (the “loud” 10%) who may hold extreme views may lead to the formation of a “trust deficit model”
estimates.notes: Meets R1 (group 10% of users AND their share 82% of MINVS content both stated). Two caveats for the adjudicator: the concentrated content is MINVS, i.e. misinformation OR negative vaccine stance combined, not misinformation alone; and the 10% cut-off is taken from prior work rather than derived, with no stated rule for who counts as 'vocal'. The value is 'over 82%', recorded as 82 (a lower bound). The sentence begins 'Our analysis revealed that ...', hyphenated across a line break in the PDF text, so the quote starts after that clause.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Not extracted: 446,400 tweets (26.5%) classified as expressing a NEGATIVE VACCINE STANCE - an attitude, not misinformation, so out of scope on its own. (2) Not extracted: the account-type breakdown 4,894 (8%) malicious bots, 8,628 (14%) normal bots, 47,038 (78%) non-bots of 60,560 accounts. The 8% is arguably a SHARING actor_share ('share of accounts that spread misinformation'), but the class is defined by automation AND a MINVS penalty score, so it is a bot prevalence rather than a clean 'users who shared misinformation' share; an adjudicator may want it. (3) Not extracted: engagement shares by account type with THL (non-bot 86%, bot 12%, malicious bot 6%) - actor composition, not misinformation content. (4) Not extracted: 24 of the top 100 accounts that mentioned THL were malicious bots, vs 1 of the top 100 mentioners overall - a count-based concentration statement that fails R1 (no share of activity attached). (5) Not extracted: THL network shares (retweeted by 2,898 accounts = 3.7% of 76,815 distinct accounts, ~5% of retweet interactions; 8,060 accounts = 15% of 54,754 mentioned accounts; 317,582 of 700,753 mentions = 45%) - reach of a reliable source, not misinformation. (6) Network structure statistics (density, diameter, reciprocity, assortativity per network) carry no prevalence share. (7) The Online Appendix (Tables 1-3, Figs 1-5) is not in this text file and may contain the classifier performance metrics and further per-period shares.

rob.design: Keyword-sampled Twitter census: 1,683,700 Finnish-language tweets from 60,560 accounts, collected via AcademictwitteR with 147 query keywords built from 14 Finnish corona/vaccine terms, 1 Dec 2019 - 24 Oct 2022. Content coding: 4,150 randomly sampled tweets manually annotated by four Finnish-speaking research assistants over six training rounds using a pre-defined vaccine-stance codebook and the Memon and Carley misinformation codebook (adapted to 2022, supported by fact-checking sites including THL); Krippendorff's alpha = 0.693 (stance) and 0.668 (misinformation), the latter at the bare minimum the authors cite as acceptable. A fine-tuned FinBERT model then labelled the remaining 1.68M tweets; no accuracy/F1 reported in the main text. Bots identified with Botometer v4 (CAP >= 0.804); malicious bots by an author-defined penalty score > 0.5. Authors note Twitter users are not representative of the Finnish population and that only tentative conclusions can be drawn.
rob.item6_quote: In this context, misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information that is intentionally or unintentionally disseminated, while a negative vaccine stance is defined as the intentional avoidance of vaccination, regardless of the reason for the avoidance.
rob.item10_quote: The misinformation classification model further identified 460,087 tweets (27.3%) as containing misinformation.
